driver_desc: the GLP-1 DEMAND SHIFT — incretin (GLP-1/GIP) therapy at population scale re-shaping FOOD AND BEVERAGE consumption: users eat materially less by volume and re-weight what they do eat toward protein and satiety, so demand moves AWAY from high-volume discretionary calories and TOWARD protein-dense, portion-controlled and satiety-positioned products. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the sub-structure tag says which side a name sits on — this is deliberate: a single company can be suppressed in one category and helped in another (a nutrition portfolio whose snacking brands face volume decline while its protein brands face a tailwind), and a one-sided driver would mis-grade exactly those names. The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. The scan decides which; a wording that pre-excluded the category would defeat the classifier it is meant to configure.
